sql-database-dtu-small-levels-cpu.title: Basic, S0, S1 and S2 provide less than one vCore
sql-database-dtu-small-levels-cpu.body: This estimate uses a DTU level of Basic, S0, S1 or S2. Microsoft states these levels provide less than one vCore of CPU, so for CPU-intensive workloads a level of S3 or higher is recommended.

citation.source: DTU-based purchasing model overview - Azure SQL Database
citation.quote: The Basic, S0, S1 and S2 service objectives provide less than one vCore (CPU). For CPU-intensive workloads, a service objective of S3 or greater is recommended.

sql-database-dtu-no-reservation.title: DTU databases cannot use reserved capacity
sql-database-dtu-no-reservation.body: This estimate uses the DTU purchasing model and you plan to keep it for a year or longer. Microsoft states that reserved instance pricing is only available in the vCore purchasing model, so compare a reserved vCore estimate for a steady workload.

citation.source: vCore purchasing model - Azure SQL Database
citation.quote: Reserved instance pricing is only available for vCore purchasing model.

sql-database-dtu-elastic-pool.title: Several DTU databases may be cheaper in an elastic pool
sql-database-dtu-elastic-pool.body: This estimate has two or more DTU databases. Microsoft says the more databases you add to a pool, the greater the savings, and savings are possible with as few as two S3 databases, so compare an elastic pool for databases with different usage peaks.

citation.source: Elastic pools help you manage and scale multiple databases in Azure SQL Database
citation.quote: Depending on your application utilization pattern, it's possible to see savings with as few as two S3 databases.
